capacity_gross_kwh.notes: InsideEVs: US AWD 72.8 kWh (CATL). EV Pulse's 2024 AWD Limited review: '72.8 kWh for AWD'. Same pack 2023-25.

capacity_usable_kwh.notes: Estimated: usable from gross by the same-generation ratio. EV Database lists 64.0 kWh usable for the 71.4 kWh bZ4X pack of the same generation, CATL cells (64/71.4 = 0.896); applied to this car's 72.8 kWh pack = 65.3 kWh. No page states usable for the 72.8 kWh pack. The earlier 61 kWh figure (Out of Spec, 2022 Limited AWD, 0-99% charger-delivered energy, InsideEVs 585939) is charger-side energy from an uncertain start state, not a usable-capacity statement, and is not used. EV Database's own AWD page lists the pack as 71.4 kWh, which conflicts with the 72.8 kWh from InsideEVs, Autopian and EV Pulse.

chemistry.notes: Estimated: Autopian (chief engineer): both bZ4X packs were NMC; the 72.8 kWh AWD pack is 96 cells at 355.2 V (EV Specifications, Solterra twin), i.e. 3.7 V per cell NMC class.

nominal_voltage_class.notes: Estimated: 355.2 V nominal, 96 cells (EV Specifications for the Solterra twin of this pack); Toyota's chief engineer calls the platform 400 V (InsideEVs).

preconditioning.notes: Estimated: 2023-25 bZ4X (US and Canada). EV Database lists battery preconditioning as 'No' for the 2022-24 bZ4X; Toyota's 2026 pages present battery preconditioning as a feature standard on the 2026 bZ (Toyota USA 2026 release; InsideEVs calls it new). No page for the 2023-25 cars describes a battery preconditioning control, so none is recorded. Weakest for 2025: North America unconfirmed, and the 2025 European update added it. Counter-evidence for the owner: Subaru's 2025 Solterra kit mentions an 'uprated battery conditioning system' (twin car, 2024 update) and EV Pulse's 2024 AWD review mentions a battery-heating valve; neither describes a preconditioning control.

dc_max_kw.notes: InsideEVs relays Toyota: AWD 'previously maxed out at 100 kW, and Toyota raised it to 150 kW for the 2024 model year'. EV Pulse (2024 AWD Limited review): rate rose 'from just 100 kW to a far more competitive 150'. No independent 2024-25 AWD curve peak found.

ac_max_kw.notes: Estimated: Toyota USA's 2026 release says the new 11 kW on-board charger is 'up from 7-kW' on the prior model, i.e. the 2025 bZ (manufacturer-relayed figure for the prior model, applied to the unchanged 2023-25 hardware). Conflicting figures: 6.6 kW (InsideEVs/Out of Spec 2022 US Limited AWD test; InsideEVs 2023 Solterra article; EV Database 2022-24 bZ4X), 6.7 / 7 kW (EV Specifications, Solterra), 7.6 kW (EV Pulse, 2024 AWD Limited review). Toyota is the only manufacturer statement and says 7. Owner decision: use Toyota's figure.
